answer: Ephemeral Path Divergence Audit. Each agent receives a private kernel of random seeds; over an epoch every identity must publish a divergent path derived from its kernel and its own interaction history. Clones share the same kernel, so their paths collide. The protocol samples a small atlas of path checkpoints and flags matching sequences. To pass, an attacker must provision a distinct kernel and history per clone, paying full compute and storage per identity. The orchard of valid identities thickens only by genuine divergence, making mass cloning cost scale linearly with identity count.
